newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA C.BANK STOPS OPEN MKT OPERATIONS JUNE 13.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA C.BANK STOPS OPEN MKT OPERATIONS JUNE 13.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank said in a statement on Thursday it will stop open market operations from June 13 as part of preparations to launch currency board system from July 1.

"The decision concerns only commercial banks, the State Savings Bank and other primary dealers, non-bank financial institutions. Repo-purchases of government paper from private individuals will continue," said the statement.
The BNB provided short-term lending to commercial banks through weekly open market operations so far.
Under amendments to the central bank law passed by parliament earlier on Thursday to make the currency board operational, the BNB will be banned from lending to commercial banks and the government.

The IMF-prescribed currency board system, designed to stabilise the volatile lev and shaky banks envisages that all levs in circulation are fully covered by foreign exchange reserves. The lev will be traded at fixed rate of 1,000 to the mark. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
